paper.title: Evolution in Simulation: AI-Agent School with Dual Memory for High-Fidelity Educational Dynamics
paper.central_claim: The AAS Zero-Exp mechanism (dual experience/knowledge memory with short/long-term tiers and an experience-reflection-optimization cycle) lets simulated school agents evolve toward high-fidelity educational behavior.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model_type is the controller-assigned type.

rationale: Domain memory-agent app; memory-off control and blind vote exist, but single-stream, weak ROUGE proxy, no gate, no stats, no cost.

evidence.quote: AAS constructs the Zero-Exp strategy, employs a continuous "experience-reflection-optimization" cycle, grounded in a dual memory base comprising experience and knowledge bases and incorporating short-term and long-term memory components.
evidence.support_explanation: Central mechanism: dual (experience/knowledge) x (ST/LT) memory with a reflection cycle.

evidence.quote: first, there is a lack of systematic modeling of the teaching process, and second, LLM agents struggle to accurately simulate the behaviors and interactions of diverse participants in educational settings.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap: domain simulation fidelity, not a fixed non-weight harness component.

evidence.quote: In light of this, this study will build upon the logic of the AI agent town and Agent Hospital
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbors named: Generative Agents and Agent Hospital; no head-to-head comparison.

evidence.quote: The contents of both the experience and knowledge bases are stored and managed within a vector database.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistence substrate: vector DB, cosine-similarity retrieval.

evidence.quote: the retrieval process of the Zero-Exp mechanism is designed to prioritize accessing relevant information from the agent's short-term memory.
New insights, facts, or optimized strategies derived from the interaction or internal reasoning are added to the Knowledge Memory Base.
evidence.support_explanation: Write path: LLM-derived insights appended to the knowledge base; no external admission test stated.

evidence.quote: Agent's reflection or changes in understanding resulting from the interaction and memory updates are also used to dynamically update aspects of their internal Role Setting (e.g., teaching methods, study habits).
evidence.support_explanation: Second retained object: the role-setting prompt is rewritten from reflection.

evidence.quote: Finally, this generated data underwent rigorous expert modification, reorganization, and reordering by educational experts to produce the complete and final interaction dataset, serving as the ground truth for evaluation and iteration.
evidence.support_explanation: Single curated 5-day dataset is both reference and iteration driver; role of reference in the loop is not specified.

evidence.quote: For automated evaluation, we compared the agent's generated response to a reference ground truth answer using the average ROUGE-L
evidence.support_explanation: Primary metric is ROUGE-L overlap with curated text.

evidence.quote: We recruited nine educational experts to evaluate these QA pairs.
evidence.support_explanation: Blind expert preference vote over 4 groups, 50 QA per checkpoint.

evidence.quote: The full model (ID 1), incorporating both the dual KB/EB structure and the ST/LT hierarchy, achieves the highest ROUGE-L scores, reaching peaks around 0.51-0.55 in the later stages.
Comparing ID 9 with any configuration using an external memory base (IDs 1-8) shows a substantial performance gap, demonstrating the fundamental benefit of external memory.
Notably, the full model's perceived realism approaches and stabilizes near that of the standard group (ID 0) in the later stages (from 60%).
evidence.support_explanation: Human blind vote: memory agent approaches expert reference.

evidence.quote: evaluation is performed periodically during the iterative process.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation interleaved with memory accumulation on the same stream (prequential).

evidence.quote: Firstly, the current simulation scale is relatively limited, involving only 50 agents (10 teachers and 40 students) over a 5-day period.
the fidelity of the simulation is also dependent on the quality and diversity of the initial expert-curated dataset used for evaluation and guiding the initial evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede the curated dataset guides evolution as well as evaluation.
Dual-vs-unified claim; Table 3 (Qwen3-235B) shows ID2 >= ID1 at 10-15% checkpoints, so 'consistently' is overstated.

claims.text: Full Zero-Exp memory yields higher-fidelity agent behavior than ablated memory configurations over the simulation.

G.reason: Gap is domain-application (teaching-process modeling, role fidelity); no fixed non-weight component identified; neighbors Generative Agents/Agent Hospital named but no residual vs their experience mechanisms.

M.reason: Concrete dual-memory + reflection + role-update design with prompts in appendix, but no explanation why dual/ST-LT should beat simple reflection memory; causal story thin.

X.reason: Write/read path described, but no admission gate, conflict/staleness handling, pruning, versioning or rollback; how short-term salience is chosen is left to the agent; role of ground-truth data in the loop unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: ROUGE-L against a Gemini-generated then expert-edited reference is a weak proxy for realism; expert vote helps but is one blind preference round that includes the reference itself.

E.causality.reason: 9-config grid isolates memory on/off, dual vs unified, ST/LT across three backbones; no literature memory baseline (e.g., reflection memory), role-update module not ablated, ID2 vs ID1 noisy.

E.holdout.reason: Only temporal prequential structure on one 5-day stream; no held-out scenario/population, no leakage audit of whether reference actions enter memory (A2: ground-truth-in-loop risk).

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes stated (50 QA/checkpoint, 500 total) and some non-monotone results shown, but single run per config, no seeds/CI/agreement stats on expert votes.

E.cost.reason: No token/call/latency/memory-growth cost reported for the memory pipeline.
